text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Parliament passed a bill on Tuesday on the circulation of securities, investment services and the securities stock exchange. @
- Outgoing Welfare Minister Gyorgy Szabo said he had failed to persuade his own staff to accept his argument that a HUF 20-25 billion injection capital would be needed to stabilise the health sector.

- Akos Birtalan, representative of the Democratic Federation of Hungarians in Romania, will receive the post of minister of tourism in the new Romanian government, while Gyorgy Tokay, will head a national minorities division or state secretariat as a minister without portfolio. @
- Hungarian foreign affairs spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi said that the Foreign Ministry is viewing the current domestic policy developments in Belarus with a great degree of alarm.
- The stock exchange brokerage firm Dunainvest Tokeugynokseg Kft. has taken over the clientele of brokerage Co-Nexus Ertekhaz, which suspended operations last week.
- The Hungarian railways are expected to transport a total of 43.8 million tonnes of goods this year, as opposed to the targeted 48 million tonnes. @

- The Gyor-Moson-Sopron County Police Department has begun an investigation against Graboplast Holding member Grabo Kft in Gyor. The company is suspected of placing environmentally hazardous waste in a Graboplast truck.
- The Buda Central District Court has found the National Police Department guilty of violating the civil rights of entrepreneur Gyorgy Klapka by giving out his companies' data to German police.
- The body of Hungarian Ambassador Antal Annus has been found and identified as among those killed in a hijacked Ethiopian airlines jet which crashed off the Comoro Islands. @
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Parliament passed the amendment to the supplementary budget Tuesday, under which the health and pension insurance funds will close this year with a combined deficit of HUF 60.1 billion, instead of the originally set HUF 17.8 billion.

- Hospitals in Budapest and a total of 14 hospitals in the provinces have submitted appeals on separate bases to the National Health Insurance Fund protesting against the reduction of beds as called for under the law.
- The National Bank of Hungary will pay back debts before maturity to a total value of $1 billion in the next six months. @
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Free Democrat Tamas Bauer and privatisation minister Judit Csiha came to a preliminary agreement on proposals to be submitted regarding the act on privatisation.
NEPSZAVA
- The Metropolitan Court is set to try the case of lawyer Marta Tocsik on December 11.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The bill on next year's budget suggests that state subsidies for churches will be 50 percent higher next year than in 1996. @
- Tamas B., head of a security company, has been detained by Budapest police in connection with the recent spate of hand grenade attacks.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The Hungarian Post Office posted operational revenues of HUF 46 billion last year and projects sales of HUF 50 billion this year.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
